briefs.title: Iran Talks Ride a Fraying Truce, Abu Dhabi Next, Mississippi Waits on Affidavits
briefs.bluf: Iran is still the center of gravity: Qatar says Washington and Tehran are each reviewing a mediators' draft, Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz within two days of a deal and leave nuclear issues for later, while a reported US strike on Qeshm Island and continued tanker hits show the truce fraying. Ukraine, Russia and the US meet in Abu Dhabi November 10 to 11 for the first formal round since February; the Kremlin says preparing for talks does not limit its operations. Mississippi's Senate race remains uncalled, with Scott Colom 43 votes ahead in the latest count and an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 affidavit ballots still to process. In Israel, the opposition has rallied behind Gadi Eisenkot and Isaac Herzog must name someone to form a government by November 11. Taiwan logged its busiest day of Chinese military flights this year as the PLA's drill season opens.
briefs._s: iran talks ride a fraying truce, abu dhabi next, mississippi waits on affidavits iran is still the center of gravity: qatar says washington and tehran are each reviewing a mediators' draft, tehran offers to reopen hormuz within two days of a deal and leave nuclear issues for later, while a reported us strike on qeshm island and continued tanker hits show the truce fraying. ukraine, russia and the us meet in abu dhabi november 10 to 11 for the first formal round since february; the kremlin says preparing for talks does not limit its operations. mississippi's senate race remains uncalled, with scott colom 43 votes ahead in the latest count and an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 affidavit ballots still to process. in israel, the opposition has rallied behind gadi eisenkot and isaac herzog must name someone to form a government by november 11. taiwan logged its busiest day of chinese military flights this year as the pla's drill season opens. mississippi senate seat comes down to affidavit ballots democrat scott colom led republican sen. cindy hyde-smith by 43 votes in the latest count reported by the mississippi free press, out of nearly 1 million cast. colom's campaign estimated 10,000 to 15,000 affidavit ballots (the provisional ballots voters cast when their registration is in question) were still outstanding. hyde-smith's campaign says it is confident she wins once every legally cast ballot is counted; colom has sent lawyers to watch county officials. mississippi has no recount law, so any fight would be over which ballots count, in court. why so many affidavit ballots: 230,000 voters flagged inactive secretary of state michael watson flagged about 230,000 registrations as inactive this cycle, using a commercial credit data program for the first time to clean the rolls. those voters could still vote, but only by affidavit ballot. supporters of the cleanup say accurate rolls protect elections; critics say it pushed eligible voters into a slower, contestable process. harrison county, on the coast, says it will not count affidavits until november 10. mississippi democrats challenge desoto county precinct problems on election night the state democratic party went to court over desoto county precincts it says opened late, had very long waits and ran short of regular and affidavit ballots. county officials' response was not collected this run. montana: republican kurt alme wins senate seat ap called montana's senate race for republican kurt alme on wednesday. it is one of the few republican pickups or holds in a cycle democrats otherwise dominated. michigan: abdul el-sayed wins open senate seat progressive democrat abdul el-sayed won michigan's senate race over republican mike rogers, according to gray tv reporting. rogers had made election integrity claims during the campaign that fact checkers disputed. qatar: both sides are reviewing a mediators' draft qatar's foreign ministry spokesman majed al-ansari said the us and iran are each reviewing proposals put forward by the mediators, that differences remain and talks continue. foreign minister abbas araghchi has floated reopening the strait of hormuz within two days of a deal and leaving nuclear issues to a second phase. secretary of state marco rubio says talks have never stopped and washington is open to a diplomatic solution. us strikes qeshm island; irgc says it downed two us drones drop site news reported a us strike on iran's qeshm island, at the mouth of the strait of hormuz, on november 3, and an irgc claim that it captured two us surveillance drones over the island. us officials had not publicly detailed the strike in sources collected this run. tanker strikes: iran claims many, ukmto confirms few the irgc navy keeps reporting multiple tankers hit each day. the british military's ukmto center confirmed only one strike late on november 3: the barbados flagged tanker grit, which trade sources describe as part of the shadow fleet and chinese owned since june. iran's tasnim agency said three tankers hit mines after entering unauthorized lanes with transponders off. treasury: no new oil loaded at iran's terminals since august 25 a us treasury report shared with axios found no new crude loaded onto tankers at iran's terminals since august 25 and called iran's economy crippled, though not near collapse. the white house frames this as pressure working; iranian officials say it will not force them to give up the stockpile first. inside iran: student sit in, execution fears, and a bomb debate in the open students at the university of tehran held a sit in on november 3, chanting against both war and bloodshed. iran international reports three protesters face imminent execution and that open debate about building a nuclear weapon is gaining ground on official platforms. iran international is an opposition leaning outlet based in london; tehran calls it hostile media. araghchi: any talks would cover only the nuclear issue iran's official news agency irna quoted araghchi on november 4 saying any negotiations with the united states would focus solely on the nuclear file, which sits awkwardly with his own two phase plan that defers it. tehran has not explained the difference. opposition lines up behind eisenkot; herzog must name someone by november 11 opposition leaders including naftali bennett, yair lapid, avigdor liberman and yair golan agreed to recommend gadi eisenkot to president isaac herzog and promised a national emergency government. netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats and eisenkot's 48; with arab led parties the anti netanyahu side reaches 67, but several opposition leaders have said they will not govern with them. netanyahu says he wants a broad national government. the knesset is sworn in november 10; the nominee then gets 28 days, plus a possible 14. rafah crossing blocked to aid and commercial goods a senior palestinian source involved in negotiations told drop site news that the rafah crossing was blocking humanitarian aid, commercial goods, food, fuel and cooking gas from entering gaza by the egyptian route. israeli and egyptian explanations were not collected this run. abu dhabi talks november 10 to 11: what is on the table steve witkoff says the us will mediate working level talks covering postwar security, de escalation, humanitarian steps and ending the war. reporting points to an energy and maritime ceasefire, prisoner exchanges and the return of ukrainian children taken to russia. it is the fourth formal round this year and the first since february, when the iran war froze the process. witkoff and jared kushner are expected to lead the us side. kremlin: preparing talks does not mean limiting operations kremlin spokesman dmitry peskov said preparing for the talks implies no commitment to limit military operations, and that every ukrainian strike would get what he called a fully justified response. aide yury ushakov called the meeting decisive and said moscow will not invite europeans. merz: russia has yet to engage seriously; europe not at the table german chancellor friedrich merz, hosting volodymyr zelensky in berlin, said russia has not seriously engaged on a ceasefire. european governments want a seat but are unlikely to be in abu dhabi. zelensky hopes the talks open the way to a leaders meeting with putin. possible trump, xi and putin meeting at apec in shenzhen trump, xi jinping and putin may hold three way talks on the sidelines of apec in shenzhen on november 18 and 19, according to al jazeera. no government has confirmed it. spain: sánchez reshuffles cabinet after transport minister quits over train crashes prime minister pedro sánchez reshuffled his cabinet after the transport minister resigned over a series of train crashes, per a reuters world summary. taiwan reports year's highest single day of pla air activity and 100 plus ships taiwan's defense ministry counted 49 pla aircraft sorties in the 24 hours to 6am november 3, the highest one day total this year, falling to 22 the next day. security chief joseph wu said more than 100 chinese navy and coast guard ships were spread across the western pacific, including the liaoning carrier group drilling in the philippine sea. taiwan has warned that november and december are the pla's peak drill season. china's central bank and regulators meet on stock support after a record 12 week slide chinese authorities were set to meet on supporting the stock market after a record 12 straight weeks of declines, according to market reporting. beijing's new export controls hit tunnel boring machines, with india in view china's newest export controls cover construction equipment including tunnel boring machines, which indian business press reads as a trade weapon against india's infrastructure buildout. asean leaders summit with the us in manila november 15 to 18 the us and asean leaders summit in manila will be the first since 2024 and trump's first, per a reuters world summary. north korea condemns new us sanctions north korea's foreign ministry condemned unilateral us sanctions, state news agency kcna reported on november 5. cambodia warns sea travelers as two storms approach cambodia urged sea travelers to be highly cautious from november 6 to 15 as two storms approach. bangladesh: garment unrest shuts 529 factories garment worker protests over pay shut 529 factories and put export orders at risk; the government formed a six member wage board, but thousands kept demonstrating. law 186 takes effect monday: what actually changes law 186, published november 2 in the official gazette, takes effect november 9 and cuts cuba's central state bodies from 27 to 21: 20 ministries plus the central bank. it merges portfolios, for example a new ministry of environment, habitat and water resources covering housing, water and the land registry, and ends a standalone internal commerce ministry. ministers have 30 days to file work schedules and up to a year to finish mergers. the text sets no job cut numbers and no wage changes, and a transitional provision addresses the ration book. rubio presses venezuela to follow a phased transition plan secretary of state marco rubio met venezuelan foreign minister oliver blanco on november 2 and urged caracas to follow the us phased plan toward a democratic transition. rubio's january plan has three stages: stabilization, recovery and reconciliation, then elections. pope leo keeps a demanding south america schedule after surgery the vatican says pope leo's november 6 to 17 tour stays unchanged, weeks after the 71 year old pontiff's lung surgery. election week false claims spread on both sides ap fact focus tracked false and misleading claims about ballots and procedures before election day. a fabricated trump post claiming republicans won everywhere was traced to a parody page. the daily dot noted conservative accounts pushing machine glitch fraud claims and left leaning accounts pushing their own conspiracy theories. fridge attacks: second wave hit seven countries; still no attribution overnight into november 2, attackers switched supermarket refrigeration controllers into defrost mode in belgium, the netherlands, sweden, luxembourg, ireland, estonia and beyond, heating some units to 50°c. it followed a first wave in france on october 11 and 12. france's cyber agency ties both to internet exposed danfoss and copeland/dixell controllers, many no longer updated. belgian federal prosecutors opened a case. no government or group has named a culprit. iran, bangladesh, israel: protest week abroad students sat in at the university of tehran, garment workers kept protesting in bangladesh, and thousands rallied in tel aviv over coalition choices. details are in the country sections. sudan: a year after el fasher fell, civilians still detained and tortured amnesty international says survivors of the 18 month rsf siege of el fasher still face detention, torture and little aid a year after the city fell in october 2025. india made hiv prevention shot approved approval of an india made hiv prevention injection raised hopes of cheaper access in poorer countries, business standard reported. stocks fell thursday on ai valuations and the worst october for layoffs in 20 plus years wall street closed lower on november 6 on tech valuation worries and a jump in job cuts tied to ai. challenger counted 153,074 announced cuts in october, the most for that month in more than two decades. the nasdaq 100 entered a correction on november 2, more than 10% below its october 6 record. oil fell sharply on iran talk hopes early in the week brent dropped about 7.5% to about $105 on november 2 as qatar mediated talks raised hopes; wti fell below $97. thursday and friday figures were not verified this run. lee county clerk opens east lee office monday the lee county clerk and comptroller opens a new east lee county office in lehigh acres at 8:30am on november 9. no, the fbi did not raid a houston office and find fraudulent ballots fbi houston said posts claiming it ran an election related raid on november 2 that found fraudulent ballots were false and that no such operation took place. the 'all 50 states' trump post came from a parody page a screenshot of a supposed trump post saying republicans had won everywhere and counting should stop was traced to a facebook page that labels its content satire; no matching post exists on his account. a cheaper hiv prevention shot made in india an india made hiv prevention injection won approval, raising hopes it can reach people in poorer countries who could not afford the originals. the fbi raided a houston office on november 2 and found fraudulent ballots. trump posted that republicans already won all 50 states and counting should stop. mississippi's voter roll cleanup was designed to suppress democratic and black voters. russia is behind the european supermarket fridge attacks. a scientist predicted the world ends on friday, november 13, 2026. qatar says both sides are reviewing a mediators' draft. drop site reports a us strike on qeshm island on november 3 and an irgc drone claim. ukmto confirmed one tanker strike (grit) against iranian claims of many. agenda for abu dhabi firmed up: energy and maritime pause, prisoners, children. kremlin says no limit on operations and no europeans. mississippi is down to affidavit ballots, many from 230,000 voters flagged inactive; latest lead 43 votes for colom. montana went to republican kurt alme, michigan to democrat abdul el-sayed. 49 pla sorties in a day and 100 plus ships at sea, the highest air count this year. law 186 enters into force november 9; ministers get 30 days for schedules and a year to merge bodies. fridge attack second wave reached at least seven countries; belgian prosecutors investigating; still no attribution. benjamin netanyahu gadi eisenkot democrats republicans briefs.title: Markets Turn on the AI Buildout, Iran Talks Stall on Sequencing, Two Senate Seats Still Open
briefs.bluf: The Iran war is still the defining factor. Three more tankers were damaged near Qatar on November 5, Trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while Qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and IAEA access for reopening Hormuz. Wall Street had its worst day in years: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the Nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since March 2020, on fears that a Democratic Congress slows the AI buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. Democrats hold 54 Senate seats with Mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and Alaska (ranked choice tally November 18) still open, and a Justice Department suit over a second Dan Sullivan on the Alaska ballot is the main certification risk. In Cuba, Yoani Sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the Law 186 government overhaul takes effect November 9. Ukraine talks move to Abu Dhabi November 10 to 11 after a White House event marking the Oleshky humanitarian truce.
briefs._s: markets turn on the ai buildout, iran talks stall on sequencing, two senate seats still open the iran war is still the defining factor. three more tankers were damaged near qatar on november 5, trump said he may have to destroy the rest of the country, and a carrier group is heading to the region, while qatar shuttles a plan that trades lifting the blockade and iaea access for reopening hormuz. wall street had its worst day in years: the nasdaq fell 5.5% and the nasdaq 100 6.4%, its worst session since march 2020, on fears that a democratic congress slows the ai buildout; futures point to a partial rebound this morning. democrats hold 54 senate seats with mississippi (a margin of about 138 votes) and alaska (ranked choice tally november 18) still open, and a justice department suit over a second dan sullivan on the alaska ballot is the main certification risk. in cuba, yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours, but two other independent journalists remain jailed and the law 186 government overhaul takes effect november 9. ukraine talks move to abu dhabi november 10 to 11 after a white house event marking the oleshky humanitarian truce. two senate races still open democrats hold 54 seats and flipped iowa, kansas, maine, ohio, north carolina, south carolina and texas. in mississippi, democrat scott colom leads sen. cindy hyde-smith 49.0% to 48.9% with about 3,600 mail ballots left; certification is due november 13. in alaska, mary peltola leads sen. dan sullivan 48.2% to 47.9% with ranked choice results due november 18. doj suit could stall alaska certification the justice department sued in october to block certification if peltola wins by less than the vote total of a second, unaffiliated candidate named daniel j. sullivan, arguing voters may have been confused. trump said he ordered the suit and has urged prosecuting peltola. legal scholars say the statute does not let doj enjoin a state certification. judge pauses the trump arch; la picks a new mayor a federal judge blocked construction of the planned arch for 14 days. in los angeles, nithya raman defeated mayor karen bass. in california, gov. newsom commuted 548 death sentences. more tankers hit; trump weighs a heavier strike the irgc said three more tankers were damaged november 5, two by mines and one by fire. ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump said he would rather not destroy the rest of the country but may have to, met his national security team, and spoke with the qatari emir, who urged restraint. a carrier group is heading to the region via singapore. diplomacy stuck on sequencing iran sent a nuclear proposal through qatar that it will discuss only after the us meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions and paying war reparations. a qatari draft reported by axios has the us lift the blockade and release some frozen funds and iran invite the iaea to bombed sites on day one, with hormuz reopening on day two and nuclear talks on the enriched uranium stockpile after that. iranian sources told reuters another us attack is more likely than a deal. tehran leans on the region foreign minister araghchi called his counterparts in the uae, qatar, saudi arabia, turkey, pakistan, oman and egypt. parliament speaker qalibaf mocked vice president vance as a losing gambler after vance blamed the war for the midterm losses. israel: herzog weighs who forms the next government after the october 27 election left netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and gadi eisenkot's at 48, president herzog began consultations, meeting the smallest parties first. eisenkot was expected to have more endorsements than netanyahu. the election commission reviewed 9,069 polling stations and found no fraud. white house marks the oleshky truce melania trump hosted russian envoy kirill dmitriev and ukraine's david arakhamia to mark the six day humanitarian ceasefire in occupied oleshky (october 27 to november 1). more than 750 people were evacuated; russia refused to extend it. president trump met dmitriev but not the ukrainians and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks next week witkoff and kushner lead the us side at three way talks in abu dhabi november 10 to 11. german chancellor merz hosts a coalition of the willing summit november 19. russia holds about 80% of donetsk. yoani sánchez released; two journalists still held yoani sánchez, director of 14ymedio, was released after more than nine hours in custody. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet, arrested november 2, and henry constantín, jailed since september 16, remain detained. rsf, the inter american press association and amnesty international condemned the detentions. law 186 reshapes the government from november 9 the law, approved july 30 and published november 2 in the gaceta oficial, cuts the cabinet to 20 ministries plus the central bank and merges commerce, construction and agriculture into fewer bodies. officials present it as streamlining; critics see a shuffle that leaves the economic model untouched. protest count stays high the observatorio cubano de conflictos logged 542 protests and complaints in october and 85 repressive events. transition quiet no new annulment filings or street mobilization found. lula takes office january 1. pope leo begins south america tour the first us born pope is in uruguay november 6 to 8, argentina november 8 to 11 and peru november 11 to 17, about 50 events in 10 cities, including a return to chiclayo, where he was bishop, and a meeting with president milei. former fbi agent charged doj charged former fbi agent andrew reyes on november 5. details of the charges were not collected this cycle. election claims fade, alaska suit gives them a new hook rigging claims about the midterms have lost momentum as most losers conceded, but the doj suit over the second dan sullivan gives the "stolen seat" framing a new focus in alaska. fridge hacks: still no attribution no group has claimed or been named for the attacks on supermarket refrigeration controllers. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called them deliberate. the danfoss and copeland flaws were disclosed by claroty august 9; forescout counted about 13,000 exposed systems. the pentagon is reviewing august freezer failures at military commissaries. mexican judge arrested in ryan wedding case a mexican judge was arrested over an alleged $2 million bribe tied to the case against ryan wedding, the former olympic snowboarder accused of running a cocaine network and ordering the killing of a federal witness. wedding was captured in mexico in january. doj launches super intelligence task force the department announced a task force on ai related crime the same day it charged a $129 million fraud marketed as a super intelligence investment. no new ofac actions found for november context: the cartel del noreste was designated october 13, venezuela's jorge rodríguez was delisted october 14, and foreign banks must exit panama's bicsa by november 14. deportations deepen school enrollment drops npr reports ice enforcement is accelerating enrollment declines in districts with large immigrant populations. doj also sued penn state over in state tuition for undocumented students. why the doomsday date keeps spreading writers revisiting the 1960 "doomsday" paper note that a specific date, a real scientific source and a friday the 13th make a claim shareable. the historian alan maceachern argues the lesson is about how confidently findings are presented. ai selloff after the election nvidia fell 9.2%, about $440 billion in value, and the largest tech stocks lost more than $1 trillion as investors priced in a congress that may slow data center and chip spending. south korea's kospi fell about 8 to 9% and halted trading. google: accept ai or lose search in schools from early 2027, gemini and search will be off by default on k-12 student accounts; schools that switch ai off entirely will also lose search. fairplay urged schools to consider other search engines. supreme court hears labor visa case november 10 department of labor v. sun valley orchards is argued monday. claim: a scientist said the world ends november 13 the date comes from a real 1960 science paper. its authors fitted a curve to population history that reached infinity in late 2026, and they picked friday the 13th partly as a joke. population growth peaked soon after and the curve stopped matching reality. hundreds leave oleshky more than 750 civilians left the occupied town during the six day truce, the largest humanitarian pause of the war in that area. the midterms were rigged through fake ballots and compromised machines democrats won by importing foreigners and registering them to vote (great replacement framing) ebola is a hoax, a western bioweapon, or a scheme for aid groups to make money a scientist predicted the world ends on friday, november 13, 2026 three more tankers damaged november 5 and ukmto reported a tanker hit by two projectiles 50 nautical miles north of madinat ash shamal, qatar. trump met his national security team and said iran would know soon enough; the nyt reports us forces are poised to resume major combat. iran sent a nuclear proposal via qatar to be discussed only after the us meets seven demands. democrats hold 54 seats. mississippi is within about 138 votes with roughly 3,600 mail ballots left and certification due november 13; alaska ranked choice results come november 18 while a doj suit seeks to block certification if peltola wins. melania trump hosted russian and ukrainian delegations (dmitriev and arakhamia) at the white house to mark the oleshky truce; more than 750 people were evacuated and russia refused an extension. trump met dmitriev and predicted a deal soon. abu dhabi talks are set for november 10 to 11. yoani sánchez was released after more than nine hours. adelth bonne gamboa of cubanet (arrested november 2) and henry constantín (jailed since september 16) remain held; rsf, iapa and amnesty condemned the detentions. law 186 was gazetted november 2 and takes effect november 9. still no attribution for the supermarket refrigeration hacks. belgium opened a prosecution and the eu called the attacks deliberate; the flaws in danfoss and copeland controllers were disclosed in august and about 13,000 systems were exposed online. no verified november activity figures collected; the story stays steady pending fresh mnd data. no new legal or street challenges found. inauguration remains january 1. benjamin netanyahu gadi eisenkot democrats republicans christopher luxon chris hipkins winston peters   alberto núñez feijóo pedro sánchez santiago abascal adama barrow  michel martelly about 16 registered candidates  bola tinubu atiku abubakar peter obi     russian deepfake campaign against democrats (matryoshka / operation overload and storm-1516) inauthentic accounts in competitive races, hitting both parties far right networks break with trump after the losses

briefs.title: Baseline Edition: A Gulf War Under Domestic Pressure, a Hybrid Campaign in Europe, and Cuba Under Strain
briefs.bluf: The defining factor this week is the collision between the US war on Iran and US domestic politics: Democrats won both chambers on November 3 and the Vice President publicly blamed the war. Washington struck Iranian targets near Hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through Gulf mediators. In Europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a Russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. Russia killed 42 people at a Ukrainian aid center days before US mediated talks on November 10 and 11. Cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. This is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here.
briefs._s: baseline edition: a gulf war under domestic pressure, a hybrid campaign in europe, and cuba under strain the defining factor this week is the collision between the us war on iran and us domestic politics: democrats won both chambers on november 3 and the vice president publicly blamed the war. washington struck iranian targets near hormuz on the eve of the vote and tankers keep burning near the strait, while talks run through gulf mediators. in europe, a wave of hoax bomb threats against flights fits the pattern of a russian linked hybrid campaign, unattributed so far. russia killed 42 people at a ukrainian aid center days before us mediated talks on november 10 and 11. cuba is under severe strain from the oil blockade and is detaining independent journalists. this is the baseline edition, so status changes are measured from here. democrats win the house and senate democrats are projected to exceed 250 house seats and hold at least 54 senate seats. alaska (peltola leads sullivan by 637 votes) and mississippi (colom leads hyde smith by about 1,100) remain too close to call. vance blames the iran war for the losses the vice president wrote that the war was the reason republicans lost. trump acknowledged gas prices hurt but said he would go to war again. house leadership reshuffle speaker johnson will not seek to lead house republicans. scalise and jordan are running for minority leader; jeffries is running for speaker when congress convenes january 3. us strikes near hormuz on the eve of the midterms limited us strikes hit around qeshm, hengam and bandar abbas. iran's supreme national security council head said the strait stays closed until us addresses its conditions: lifting the naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions and a ceasefire including lebanon. more tankers on fire east of hormuz; tanker hit off qatar iranian state media reported two more tankers on fire. separately, the british military said a tanker was struck by projectiles off qatar. iran's security chief meets putin mohsen rezaei discussed regional issues in moscow, and iran says it will supply russian gas to neighboring countries. gaza and yemen at least four palestinians were killed in gaza on november 5. in yemen's taiz, government forces say they repelled a houthi attack; the un says water production has halved and hospitals are short of fuel. aid center strike toll reaches 42 russian bunker busting bombs hit a school used as an aid hub in komyshuvakha, then the shelter where people took cover. erdogan wants direct talks with putin; italy readies aid after talks with zelenskyy, erdogan said he wants to discuss ending the war with putin. italy is finalizing a new military aid package. putin seizes japan tobacco's russian operations; drone strike hits ozon warehouse moscow took control of jti's russian business. a drone strike set an ozon warehouse ablaze in southern russia. pla activity rebounds after typhoon lull 85 sorties from october 26 to november 1, 47 into the adiz. on november 3 to 4: 22 sorties, 7 pla navy ships and 5 official ships. beijing's ai enabled influence operations ahead of taiwan's local elections taiwanese officials report ai generated content and cyberattacks aimed at polarization and lower turnout before the november 28 vote. vietnam comments on china and laos military cooperation hanoi said the cooperation should contribute to regional stability. yoani sánchez detained in havana the 14ymedio founder was held about nine hours, the third detention of an independent journalist in havana this week after cubanet's camila acosta on tuesday. the us condemned the arrests. grid at about a third of demand the une forecast 958 mw available against 2,850 mw demand on november 2, with blackouts over 20 hours a day. government reorganization takes effect november 9 law 186 cuts central state agencies from 27 to 21. reported military mobilization cibercuba reports cuba mobilizing forces amid rising tensions with the us. transition settling after contested runoff lula won 51.8% to 48.2%. flávio bolsonaro's party acknowledged the result after his annulment call; trump called it rigged. colombia ends 'total peace' congress passed president de la espriella's bill: armed group members must disarm, identify fellow members, hand over recruited minors, surrender assets and reveal links to politicians to earn reduced sentences. leaders face at least 10 years. paraguay seizes bank tied to the president central bank took over ueno bank after its capital fell below half the legal minimum; about 3 million accounts and public pension funds frozen. poland arrests four over military supplies sent to russia part of a broader pattern of sabotage and procurement networks targeting the main aid route to ukraine. hoax bomb threats hit european aviation about ten flights threatened november 3 and four prague bound planes november 5. the eu transport chief says it is too early to say whether they are linked. prc influence operations target taiwan's november 28 vote officials cite ai generated content designed to polarize and depress turnout. narrative watch: iranian leadership messaging a statement attributed to mojtaba khamenei claims iran's control of hormuz shattered the myth of american invincibility. supermarket refrigeration systems hacked across europe unidentified
